message.content: The last common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) is the most recent common ancestor of the clade **Laurasiatheria**. This ancestor was a placental mammal that lived roughly 70–80 million years ago, before the diversification of the orders Carnivora (which includes lions) and Perissodactyla (which includes zebras).
